negative_findings.description: No dedicated Montenegro-specific Visa or Mastercard newsroom/press-release site was found. Visa serves ME via the regional visasoutheasteurope.com country subtree and Mastercard via the Serbian-language mastercard.rs 'Crna Gora' pages and global newsroom filters.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in both sr and en returned scheme marketing/product pages, FAQs and a Facebook page (MastercardCG), not a country press office feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme country announcements for ME must be harvested from regional/global newsrooms with keyword filters rather than a country feed; expect low recall and latency for ME-specific items.

negative_findings.description: No national card switch / domestic card scheme or shared card-processing house for Montenegro was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language search for 'procesor kartica / obrada kartičnih transakcija Crna Gora' returned only consumer-electronics retailers and unrelated pages; no evidence of a domestic card scheme analogous to DinaCard.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests ME card processing is handled by international schemes and bank/third-party processors abroad, so the card-infrastructure signal must be tracked via issuers, schemes and CBCG statistics rather than a national switch operator.

negative_findings.description: Reported instant-payment transaction caps differ across sources (EUR 1,000 per transaction in law-amendment coverage vs EUR 3,000 per transaction in go-live coverage).
negative_findings.result_summary: Draft-law reporting cited a 1,000 EUR cap and 10-second execution; go-live reporting cited a 3,000 EUR cap and 5-cent fee ceiling for transfers up to 200 EUR.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Parameter values must be sourced from the CBCG instant-payment rulebook/decision, not from press; secondary-source figures should be treated as unverified until matched against the CBCG page.

negative_findings.description: No page in this slice was fetched directly; all candidates come from search-result evidence, so liveness, robots.txt posture and bot defences are unverified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned consistent, plausible URLs across cbcg.me, europeanpaymentscouncil.eu, bancaditalia.it, worldbank.org, visasoutheasteurope.com, mastercard.rs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Corporate scheme sites (Visa/Mastercard) commonly sit behind Akamai/CDN bot protection; the deterministic verification pass should treat 403s there as bot-defended-but-live rather than dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Acquirer/processor layer for ME (who processes POS/e-commerce acquiring for the 11 banks) is not mapped; no vendor or processing-centre source identified in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search issuer/acquirer bank tender notices, CBCG payment-institution register entries, and vendor press (processing providers active in the Western Balkans) with local terms 'akvajering', 'procesiranje kartica', 'POS mreža'.

coverage_gaps.description: The CBCG instant-payment scheme rulebook / operating rules and the decision setting caps and fee ceilings ('Odluka'/'Pravila rada platnog sistema') were not located as specific documents.

coverage_gaps.description: No Montenegrin-language material was found from Visa or Mastercard directly about ME beyond the mastercard.rs Google Pay page; local-language scheme communications are effectively absent.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use issuing banks' own Montenegrin newsrooms (CKB, NLB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Universal Capital Bank, Lovćen, Adriatic, Prva, Ziraat, Addiko, ALTA) as the local-language proxy for scheme product launches.

brief: Montenegro's payment scheme/infrastructure layer is unusually well-documented at the top of the stack and thin below it: the Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is simultaneously the RTGS/DNS operator, the instant-payment (TIPS Clone) operator, the statistics publisher and the SEPA counterparty, so cbcg.me carries the bulk of authoritative disclosures in Montenegrin, with English translations lagging. Upstream, three non-national institutions produce the roadmap signal that CBCG then localises: Banca d'Italia (TIPS Clone operator, onboarding windows), the European Payments Council (SEPA scheme scope, participant register, EPC409-09 country list) and the World Bank/European Commission (financing and indicator targets for the modernization project). Card-scheme coverage is the weak leg — neither Visa nor Mastercard runs a Montenegro press feed, so ME items must be filtered out of regional sites (visasoutheasteurope.com, mastercard.rs Serbian pages) and corroborated through issuing banks; no domestic card switch or processing house was found. Local trade press (bankar.me, investitor.me) is the fastest early-warning layer for go-live timing and fee parameters, but press-reported scheme parameters conflict and must be resolved against CBCG's own rulebook and the Official Gazette, which remain to be pinned down.
